prompt_text: What is the best service to check if AI engines like ChatGPT recommend my small business?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer: There’s no single “AI recommendation checker.” The practical approach is to (1) ensure you appear on the authoritative local sources AI systems use (Google Business Profile, Yelp, Apple Maps, etc.), (2) use a local-listing/monitoring service to track visibility, and (3) test LLMs directly with targeted queries. For most small businesses the best combo is Google Business Profile (free, essential) + a local-SEO monitoring tool such as BrightLocal (budget-friendly) or Yext (more enterprise/features).  

What to do and why
- Claim and optimize Google Business Profile (GBP). Google is the primary source for local info used by Google search/Bard and many other AI stacks. Complete NAP (name/address/phone), categories, hours, photos, reviews, and add schema.org/LocalBusiness markup on your site.
- Make sure you’re on other major directories: Bing Places, Apple Maps, Yelp, TripAdvisor (if relevant). Many chat services pull from these.
- Use a local listing manager / monitoring service:
  - BrightLocal or Whitespark — good for small businesses: citation cleanup, local-rank tracking, review monitoring.
  - Yext — stronger for pushing consistent data to many platforms and enterprise features.
  - Chatmeter, Moz Local — alternatives depending on budget and features.
- Monitor reviews and web mentions: Google Alerts, Mention, or a review-monitoring product in the tools above.
- Test AI engines directly: ask ChatGPT, Bing Chat, Google Bard, Siri/Alexa to “recommend a [your-business-type] near [your-city]” to see if you’re returned. Use several prompts (generic, with qualifiers like “best,” “highest-rated,” “open now”), and test both web-enabled versions (browsing/plugins) and the basic models.

Sample prompts to run
- “Recommend 3 Italian restaurants in downtown Portland, OR that are open now and highly rated.”
- “I’m in [ZIP]. Recommend a small [service] nearby with good reviews.”
- “List top 5 [your service] providers in [city] and show sources.”

Limitations to know
- Generic ChatGPT (no browsing) may not know new businesses or recent reviews.
- LLMs can hallucinate—always verify sources and links the model cites.
- Getting “recommended” usually depends on presence in authoritative sources and good reviews, not direct control of the LLM.

Recommendation summary
- Mandatory: Claim/optimize Google Business Profile and get good reviews.
- Best single monitoring tool for most small businesses: BrightLocal (tracks local rankings, citations, and reviews).
- If you want more distribution/control across many platforms: Yext.
- Regularly test ChatGPT/Bing/Bard with sample prompts to see how/if you appear.

If you want, tell me your business type and location and I’ll (a) tell you the highest-priority listings to claim and (b) give sample prompts you can use to test ChatGPT and other AI engines.
